Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

meet verb

by chance, or on the way

also run into, bump into, come across, go to meet, meet someone off the train

classical

Phaedr. 3.7.2–3: canī perpāstō … lupus forte occurrit
Traupman 94, 284: bump into s.o., alicui occurrere

occurrō, occurrere, occurrī, occursum

verb, third conjugation, with the dative

meet, run into; go to meet

With the dative of the person met; forte, “by chance”, makes it an accident.

Examples

  • cum mihi in silvā Gallīnāriā obviam vēnisset quaesīssemque quid agerēs, dīxit tē in lectō esse

    when [Caeparius] met me in the Gallinarian Wood and I asked how you were, he told me you were in bedCic. Fam. 9.23.1

  • canī perpāstō maciē cōnfectus lupus forte occurrit

    a wolf worn thin with hunger happened to meet a well-fed dogPhaedr. 3.7.2–3

  • quam longissimē poteris obviam nōbīs prōdeās

    come out along the road to meet us as far as you canCic. Fam. 14.5.1

Other words

  • obviam fierī (venīre) — meet (someone) on one’s way

    phrase, with the dative · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 9.23.1: cum mihi … obviam vēnisset; Traupman 94: alicui obviam fierī

  • obviam īre (prōdīre) — go to meet, go and meet (someone arriving)

    phrase, with the dative · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 14.5.1: obviam nōbīs prōdeās; M-O s.v. meet, pick up: obviam īre

See also meet, receive, arrive, hit.

SourcesLewis & Short: occurro · Lewis & Short: obviam
